```{r setup, include = FALSE}
needed <- c("FactoMineR", "fabia", "GFA", "uwot", "Rtsne")
has_all <- all(vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 96, message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE, eval = has_all)
```

This page walks through a complete multi-omics factor analysis with
**factomics**: fit several factor methods, look at the factors in
low-dimensional embeddings, cluster the samples, check which method agrees with
which, and find out what each factor means.

```{r}
library(factomics)
```

## 1. Data

factomics takes a **named list of numeric matrices, features in rows and samples
in columns**, one matrix per omics layer ("view"). All views must share the same
sample names. Here we simulate three views measured on 60 samples from three
groups, with a known set of latent factors:

```{r}
sim <- simulate_multiomics(n_samples = 60, n_groups = 3, seed = 1)
lapply(sim$data, dim)
head(sim$metadata)
```

See the [Using your own data](https://lucp12891.github.io/factomics/articles/own-data.html) article for reading your own files.

## 2. Fit factor models

`run_factor_pipeline()` runs any set of methods and returns them in one format.
`list_factor_methods()` shows what is available on your machine:

```{r}
list_factor_methods()[, c("method", "package", "installed")]
```

```{r}
res <- run_factor_pipeline(
  sim$data,
  methods = c("PCA", "MFA", "FABIA", "GFA"),
  k       = 4,
  verbose = FALSE
)
res
```

Every method has the same three slots: `scores` (samples x factors),
`loadings` (features x factors, named `view::feature`) and `meta`:

```{r}
head(res$MFA$scores, 3)
head(res$GFA$loadings, 3)
```

## 3. Attach metadata

```{r}
res <- attach_scores_metadata(res, sim$metadata, sample_col = "sample")
head(res$MFA$scores_with_meta[, c("sample", "F1", "F2", "group")], 3)
```

## 4. How much does each factor explain?

`variance_explained()` regresses each view on each method's factors, so every
method is measured on the same R^2 scale:

```{r, fig.height = 3.6}
plot_variance_explained(res)
```

## 5. Look at the factor space

Plot two factors directly, or embed the full factor space with PCA, UMAP or
t-SNE. The concatenated input data are embedded too, as a baseline:

```{r}
plot_factor_scores(res, metadata = sim$metadata, color_by = "group")
```

```{r, fig.height = 6}
emb <- embed_results(res, type = c("umap", "tsne"))
plot_embedding(emb, metadata = sim$metadata, color_by = "group")
```

## 6. Cluster the samples

`cluster_results()` clusters the samples on each method's factors and picks the
number of clusters by the mean silhouette width:

```{r}
cl <- cluster_results(res, cluster_method = "kmeans", k = 2:6)
cl
```

Because we know the true groups here, we can score each clustering with the
adjusted Rand index (1 = perfect):

```{r}
truth <- setNames(sim$metadata$group, sim$metadata$sample)
compare_clusterings(cl, truth)$vs_truth
```

```{r, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_clusters(cl, "agreement", truth = truth)
```

## 7. Interpret the factors

Which factors track the sample covariates?

```{r, fig.height = 3.6}
plot_factor_associations(res, sim$metadata)
```

Which features drive a factor?

```{r, fig.height = 5}
plot_top_loadings(res, "MFA", factor = 1, n = 20)
```

## 8. Compare the methods

`benchmark_factor_methods()` matches factors between every pair of methods
(Hungarian algorithm on the score correlations) and summarises how well they
agree:

```{r}
bm <- benchmark_factor_methods(res)
bm$summary_table_scores[, c("pair", "mean_abs_corr_scores")]
```

```{r, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 6.5}
bm$all_scores_heatmap
```

## All of it in one call

`factomics()` chains all of the above and `export_results()` writes the tables
to disk:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fx <- factomics(sim$data, metadata = sim$metadata,
                methods = c("PCA", "MFA", "FABIA", "GFA"), k = 4,
                embeddings = c("umap", "tsne"), cluster_method = "kmeans")
export_results(fx, "factomics_output")
```
